answer: Stake-bonded reputation makes each identity expensive to create and costly to lose. An agent locks a ferrous-hard deposit before its attestations carry weight, so spinning up thousands of fake identities means locking thousands of bonds. Newcomers enter through a narrow inlet, a probationary lane with limited influence, so a flood of fresh accounts cannot swamp the system at once. If an identity misbehaves its bond is slashed and its reputation lost, so every echo of the same abuse must be paid for again. One honest, long-lived identity ends up far more valuable than many disposable ones.
